objective: bound CPU streamed-expert MMID wall occupancy in a 513-ID cold P12 server prefill, without promoting instrumented timing
hypothesis: if all CPU streamed MMID intervals together occupy less than 20 percent of completion-fenced prefill time, eliminating even all of those intervals cannot explain a material prefill improvement in this workload
alternative: MMID intervals may dominate enough wall time to justify a phase-specific critical-path experiment; upload/pread overlap and marker specificity must still be resolved
workload: single synthetic 513-ID cold prompt, greedy cap 4 tokens; no prior prefix, no prompt-cache reuse
profile: P12 ngl12, ub32, slots32, full-SWA 8K, original backend; C15 differs only by optional NVTX/counter instrumentation
measurement_freeze_rule: fresh preflight must be committed before the first run; each prior receipt and idle must be committed before the next arm
conditional_run_rule: next run only if previous run passes resource/output gates; profiler only after control and plain C15 have the same four-token result
idle_admission: 300 contiguous seconds <=1 s cadence, start <=50/50/45 C, later arms match first final baseline within 5/5/3 C, <=900 s
resource_envelope: E18 18 GiB cgroup, zero swap, RSS <=16 GiB, cgroup <=16.5 GiB, GPU total <=6500 MiB, MemAvailable >=6 GiB, CPU95 warning/CPU100 stop, GPU80 and NVMe70 stop
bound_rule: sum/union of C15_CPU_STREAM_MATMUL_ID intervals across profiler run is only an optimistic upper bound for prefill removability, since it may include decode and overlap; denominator is uninstrumented control completed prefill time; if <20%, deprioritize MMID compaction for this cold513 workload; if >=20%, require phase-specific attribution before implementation
numerical_gate: greedy four-token message/finish reason equality between original and C15; full logits same-profile bitwise NOT_RUN, so diagnostic timing is never promoted
failure_policy: stop affected unit on mismatch, telemetry/guard error or profiler absence; preserve receipt, no hidden retry
